h1: Do I need a permit for a retaining wall in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Retaining Wall Permits: Four-Foot Rules and Special Permits
description: Compare the state building-code exemption with Newton's local retaining-wall zoning review and site-plan requirements.
short_answer: A retaining wall no higher than 4 feet, measured from the bottom of its footing to the top of the wall, may qualify for the state building-permit exemption if it does not support a surcharge or impound certain liquids. Newton zoning separately requires a special permit for a retaining wall 4 feet or higher, so a wall can trigger local zoning review even when it falls within the state building-code exemption.

facts.text: The state code exempts qualifying retaining walls no higher than 4 feet when height is measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall. The exemption does not apply to walls supporting a surcharge or impounding the specified classes of liquids.
Newton zoning requires a special permit for a retaining wall 4 feet or higher. The ordinance also addresses combined walls located within 25 feet of each other.
Newton Engineering reviews site plans involving retaining walls and grade alterations.

qa.q: Can a 4-foot retaining wall need a Newton special permit even if the state building code exempts it from a building permit?
qa.a: Yes. The state building-code exemption and Newton's local special-permit rule are separate requirements.
